| V1-COMPLETION-REFUND-RESTORE | **Gift-card refund restore — closes the consumer-money gap.** Certification found `refund_credit` was a dead ledger capability: `create_checkout_order` debits the gift-card ledger on redemption, but no path wrote the offsetting `refund_credit` the balance projection already counts — so refunding/cancelling a gift-card-funded order **silently destroyed the customer's redeemed balance** (`complete_order_refund` writes nothing to the gift-card ledger). Migration 174 adds `restore_gift_card_on_refund(store, order)` (SECURITY DEFINER): for each **committed** redemption on the order (FOR UPDATE) it writes a `refund_credit` entry (`amount` = redeemed, `balance_after` = projection + amount) and marks the redemption `released`. **Idempotent** (unique `gift_card.refund_credit:order:redemption` key + `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` + committed→released transition → no double credit). Wired into the `PATCH /orders/:id` cancel/refund transition (the unambiguous whole-order-reversed signal) via `db.rpc`, best-effort. Canonical `complete_order_refund`/`create_checkout_order` **untouched** (validator-pinned). New app-api proxy `gift-cards/[id]/route.ts` (GET audit + PATCH status) → **route lockstep 128→129** (domain-boundary, federation, lb6, lb12 mirror, ownership doc). Tenant isolation: every route `verifySiteOwnership`; RPCs site-scoped SECURITY DEFINER. **Verified:** api-gateway tsc 0, queue-workers tsc 0, api-client `tsc -b` 0, MCP gift-cards page + new route tsc 0 (3 pre-existing unrelated MCP errors untouched); `lb11-giftcards` (11: canonical RPCs, hash-match lifecycle close, ledger projection, RPC-only mutations, ownership, fraud, email, schemas/client, UI reveal, rollback+lockstep); money B3-B5 convergence 4/4 (redemption guard intact); launch suite 137/137; **gate 107/107 PASS**. create_checkout_order untouched. | S2-ROUTE-TEMPLATE-CLOSURE | **Closed the D3a/D3b defects; found D3c already fixed.** D3a: `resolveLiquidTemplateKey` silently substituted `bundle.templates.index` (or an arbitrary key) for any unmatched route template -- a Liquid-enabled store showed the merchant's home page (or a random other template) under any URL whose template was missing, a wrong-page bug with SEO impact. Fixed by making the function return `string \| null` (no substitution) and adding `StorefrontRenderPlan.liquidTemplateMiss: boolean` -- true only when the store runs Liquid, the route needed a specific template, the bundle has no match, AND no `fallbackSections` were supplied (a real, honest miss); false whenever real fallback content exists (the existing plain/legacy chain already prefers `fallbackSections` over its homepage-sections catch-all, so CMS/collection/shop routes now get REAL content instead of the home page on a miss, strictly better than before). ON CONFLICT (jti) DO NOTHING RETURNING id` inside a `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC (`consume_merchant_session_jti`), not a read-then-write, which would race. RLS: `ENABLE` + a `service_role`-only `FOR ALL USING(true)` policy, no `FORCE`, no tenant GUC -- explicitly justified, not silently omitted: a `merchant_session` JWT identifies a user, not a site, so there is no `site_id` to isolate by; `tenant-isolation-validator` re-run clean confirming no registry regeneration was needed. A second `SECURITY DEFINER` function, `expire_merchant_session_jti_consumptions`, mirrors `expire_inventory_reservations`'s exact shape (`141_executable_inventory_reservations.sql`) for cleanup, deleting only rows already past their own recorded `expires_at` (copied verbatim from the token's own `exp` claim at consume time), so it can never delete a still-valid record. **W3** -- wired the consumption check into `auth.ts`'s `POST /custom/sessions/create`, immediately after `tokenValidation.ok` is confirmed true and before the opaque `sessions` insert: decodes the already-cryptographically-verified token's `jti`/`exp` via `jose`'s `decodeJwt` (safe -- reads claims out of a token whose signature was already checked by the pure verifier one line above, performs no verification of its own), calls the new RPC, rejects with a new `MERCHANT_SESSION_TOKEN_ALREADY_CONSUMED` 409 on conflict. Cross-checked the steady-run minimums (35-39ms) against `S6-load-results-peak.json`'s `index/liquid` p50s across all 3 peak trials (34.6/35.24/46.25ms) -- same code, same route, warm, consistently fast; also independently re-verified S6's own claim that Liquid beat React in 2 of 3 peak trials (39.59 vs 34.6ms; 56.18 vs 46.25ms) directly against the JSON, not trusted from prose. **Corrected classification** (`docs/evidence/liquid-load/S7-verdict-correction.md`, supersedes, does not overwrite, S6's documents): peak-rate load stays GREEN; low-rate/steady moves from RED to **NOT_PROVEN** -- never adequately sampled, a different and more honest classification than measured-and-bad. Did NOT re-run the harness to "confirm" this correction, since n=5 being too small for a 95th-percentile claim is true by the definition of percentile, not by experiment -- re-running the SAME under-warmed design would only reproduce the same inadequate sample. **W2 -- instrumented before optimising, per the phase's own explicit mandate.** Added env-gated (`LB_S7_PROFILE=1`, zero cost when unset) span timing directly into `theme-renderer.ts` around `parseLiquidThemePackageBundle`, `LiquidRenderer.render()` (total), `getThemeDomPurify()` (dynamic-import span, singleton-JSDOM-window span, DOMPurify-construction span, and the await-cost distinguishing first-init from already-resolved), `createDocument`'s per-call JSDOM construction, and every `sanitizeRenderedHtml` call (purify.sanitize span + total span). First build attempt failed webpack (`node:perf_hooks` cannot bundle into a client chunk theme-renderer.ts is reachable from) -- switched to the globally-available `Date.now()`, which needs no import and works identically in both Node and browser globals, same fix pattern this file already uses for `jsdom`'s `webpackIgnore`. **CONFIRMED root cause #1, FIXED:** `getThemeDomPurify()`'s lazy dynamic `import('dompurify')`+`import('jsdom')` (194-454ms, directly timed across 2 independent fresh-process trials) plus singleton `new JSDOM(...)` window construction (34-38ms) pays ~230-493ms exactly ONCE per process lifetime, on whichever request arrives first -- proven NOT recurring (5 sequential warm curls, 3s apart, mirroring S6's own inter-arrival spacing, all fast at 32-46ms) and NOT render cost (every span after first-init measured 0-51ms). Fixed by moving the cost to server boot: new `warmupThemeDomPurify()` export (fire-and-forget, errors swallowed so a failed warmup can never crash startup -- the lazy path still retries on the next real request) called from a new `apps/storefront-runtime/src/instrumentation.ts` (Next.js's documented `register()` server-startup hook, `NEXT_RUNTIME==='nodejs'`-gated since jsdom/DOMPurify are server-only and this hook also runs at the Edge). Verified directly: warmup spans now fire during boot (`processUptimeMs~700-740`) before any HTTP request was sent; an isolation test (react/react/liquid in sequence on one fresh boot) measured 282ms/13ms/57ms -- the third request, first-ever hit to the Liquid path, is fast, confirming the Liquid-specific singleton cost is gone. Also discovered and explicitly disclosed, NOT fixed (engine-agnostic, out of scope): that same isolation test's FIRST request (React, never touches DOMPurify/JSDOM at all) also cost 282ms, dropping to 13ms on the second hit to the same route -- a generic Next.js first-hit-to-a-route cost, unrelated to theme-engine. **Fixed the harness's OWN measurement method**, per the phase's explicit instruction: replaced `liquid-load-harness.mjs`'s time-boxed `--warmup=<seconds>` with request-count-based `--warmup-requests=<N>` (default 5 per scenario), via a new `runRequestCountWarmup()` that explicitly awaits every scenario reaching its target count before the measured window can start -- structurally cannot under-warm a scenario or let a slow warmup request spill across the boundary the way S6's design could. **Corrected re-measurement, with the fix and the fixed method:** peak (10 req/s, 20s, n=33/scenario, 3 trials) confirmed GREEN and unchanged (deltas 0.6-1.8ms). Low-rate (2 req/s, 90s for n=30/scenario, 3 trials, warmup verified complete -- 5/5 every scenario every trial): **the ~500-555ms anomaly persisted on every Liquid scenario, every trial** -- ruling out Finding #1 as the (sole) cause. **New evidence changed the classification again:** in trial 3, the SAME ~536-546ms spike appeared on ALL THREE React scenarios too, correlating with a sharp system free-memory swing recorded via the harness's own `hostLoadSnapshot()` (2555->2340->719->666->2226MB across the 3 trials' before/after readings) -- a drop-then-recover shape within ~180s consistent with another process on this shared, ~90-competing-process machine, not this repository's code. Host pressure does not fully explain it either, since Liquid was elevated even in trials where React and free memory both stayed fine. **Classified NOT_ROOT_CAUSED**, deliberately not fixed -- applying a change against an unattributed confound would be exactly the "fix without a profile is a coincidence" the phase's own rules forbid; recommended re-running the (now-corrected) harness on an idle/dedicated machine as the concrete next step. **W3/W4** -- kept the profiling instrumentation in place (env-gated, zero cost disabled) rather than stripping it per its own original comment's aspiration, since the investigation closed with one confirmed-fixed and one NOT_ROOT_CAUSED finding, both of which a future re-investigation would need these exact spans for; updated that comment in place to state the actual disposition rather than a stale removal aspiration. | PHASE-T2A-FIX | Two bounded fixes on top of T2a's committed work. **W1 (announcement bar full-bleed)**: re-measured the defect first rather than trusting T2a's own prior claim — confirmed `x=16, width=343` at 375px, computed `max-width:343px`/`margin-left:16px` directly on the `.lb-announcement-bar` element itself, every ancestor full-width/x=0. Root cause was NOT what the phase brief hypothesized (T2a's own shared-rhythm rule in `liquid-theme.css` already correctly excludes `.lb-announcement-bar`) — traced instead to a **third, previously-flagged-stale surface**: `apps/storefront-runtime/src/app/globals.css` carries its own independent, never-cleaned-up duplicate of the "shared section rhythm" rule (`max-width:min(72rem, calc(100vw - 2rem))`) that separately named `.lb-announcement-bar` in its own selector list — both stylesheets are genuinely served, and since `liquid-theme.css`'s own rule for this class never set `max-width`/`margin-inline` at all, the stale `globals.css` rule leaked through uncontested. Fixed at the true source (removed `.lb-announcement-bar` from `globals.css`'s shared-rhythm list) plus an explicit, self-documenting `width:100%;max-width:none;margin-inline:0` directly on `liquid-theme.css`'s own rule as insurance and to satisfy the letter of the brief. `LIQUID_THEME_BASE_CSS` (theme-renderer.ts) was already correct — it uses an outer/inner split (`.lb-announcement-bar` full-bleed, `.lb-announcement-bar__inner` constrained) that the live markup already matches; nothing to change there. Verified via `getBoundingClientRect()` at 360/768(desktop breakpoint)/1280 on **two templates** (home + `/cart`): `x=0` and `width===document.documentElement.clientWidth` (the true full-bleed measure — `window.innerWidth` includes the scrollbar track, which no content can ever occupy; confirmed the ~6px gap at 1280 is exactly the scrollbar) on every one, `announcementBeforeHeader:true` confirmed on `/cart`. **W2/CAP-C19 (portable stylesheet reaches the browser)**: read `layout.tsx` and `composition-engine.tsx` first to find the real constraint before changing anything — `apps/store/[subdomain]/layout.tsx` is a NESTED layout (cannot render `<html>`/`<head>` itself), and `renderLiquidPlan()`'s prior `${header}${contentForLayout}${footer}` concatenation discarded `result.liquid.layoutHtml` (and with it, `content_for_header`'s injected `<style>`) specifically because nesting the full `<!doctype>` document inside a `<div>` is not valid. Mechanism chosen: `theme-renderer.ts` already had every safety primitive needed (`buildLiquidThemeHeadAssets`'s existing `sanitizeCssTokenValue` per-token stripping of `<>{};@()`, and `sanitizeRenderedHtml`'s existing `allowHeadMetadata` DOMPurify document-config pass, already used elsewhere for embed regions) — added one new function, `sanitizeLiquidHeadStyleText()`, that reuses that SAME `allowHeadMetadata` pass and extracts the sanitized `<style>` node's `.textContent` (real DOM extraction post-sanitization, not a string-slice of untrusted input), returned as a new `headStyleText` field on `LiquidRenderedTheme`. Extracted the exact assembly step that had the historical bug (`{header,contentForLayout,footer}` destructuring that silently dropped head assets) into a new, dependency-free, directly-unit-testable module (`liquid-page-assembly.ts` — kept OUT of `composition-engine.tsx` specifically because that file transitively imports `'server-only'`-guarded code that throws outside a Next.js Server Component context, confirmed by a failed first test run). The React side (`LiquidRenderedHtml`) renders `headStyleText` as a real `<style data-theme-renderer="liquid" precedence="lb-liquid-theme" href="lb-liquid-theme-head-assets">` element with a plain string child (not `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`) — `precedence` is REQUIRED for React 19's Resource-hoisting to activate (verified empirically: a first attempt without it left two un-hoisted `<style>` tags rendered in-place inside `<body>`, never reaching `<head>`; adding `precedence`+`href` fixed it, confirmed via live post-hydration DOM inspection — the tag lives under `<head>`, `media` is active not `"not all"`). | PHASE-T3 | Closed all three CAP-C20/C21/C22 findings T2b registered (product detail 404, schema-default loss, soft-404), each root-caused before being fixed. **W1 (CAP-C21, gateway)**: the single-product route destructured only `data` from the Supabase response, so any query failure collapsed into a fabricated `NOT_FOUND`. Surfaced the real error FIRST (a standalone diagnostic script against the live local Supabase instance, not the route code) before theorizing, per the phase's own instruction — the real error was PostgREST `42703 column products.short_description does not exist`, because `public-routes.ts`'s own `PRODUCT_SELECT_FULL`/`_RELATIONAL` constant referenced six columns that were never real (`short_description`, `compare_at_price`, `category_id`, `brand`, `inventory_quantity`, `dimensions` — confirmed against `\d products`; the sibling `storefront.ts` copy of the same constant already used the real names, which is why the listing endpoint worked and this one silently didn't). Fixing the column list surfaced a SECOND, independent defect: the `.or('slug.eq.<id>,id.eq.<id>')` filter always added the `id.eq.` branch even for non-uuid slugs, and Postgres rejects casting a non-uuid string to the `id` column's uuid type (`22P02`) — this alone broke every by-slug lookup regardless of defect 1. Fixed both; the route now only adds `id.eq.` when the identifier is uuid-shaped, and distinguishes PostgREST's genuine 0-row `PGRST116` (safe `NOT_FOUND`) from any other error (logged server-side as structured JSON, returned to the client as the existing `dbFailureBody()` shape — `{code:'DB_ERROR', message:'Database operation failed'}` — never the raw PostgREST error). No tenant filter (`store_id`, `is_active`) was touched or widened. **W2 (CAP-C20, theme-engine)**: found the actual gap — `renderLiquidTemplateSections` in `theme-renderer.ts` passed a composed section's raw `settings` straight into the Liquid scope with no merge against `sectionFile.schema.settings`'s declared `default` values, ever; this was a pure omission (no prior attempt at a defaults merge existed anywhere in the render path), not a bug in an existing merge. Added `applyLiquidSectionSchemaDefaults()`: for each schema field with a declared `default`, apply it only when the key is genuinely absent from `settings` (`hasOwnProperty` false) — an explicit key present with an empty string is a merchant's deliberate choice and is never overwritten. Then, having proven the fix, removed all 9 of T2b's explicit heading-value workarounds in `theme-bundle.ts` (`cart`, `customers/login`, `/register`, `/account`, `/orders`, `/order`, `/settings`, `/wishlist`, `/addresses`) back to `settings:{}` — each of the 9 values was confirmed byte-identical to its section's own schema default before removal (e.g. `cart-summary`'s `heading` default is literally `'Your cart'`, matching T2b's workaround verbatim), so removal changes nothing about what renders; proved via the regenerated committed example-bundle drift tests (`theme-examples.test.ts`) and the full 1848-test suite, not asserted. **Browser-editor verification gap, disclosed rather than fabricated**: attempted the mandated "add a section through the live theme editor" proof — created a real merchant account and store via `identity-platform`/`merchant-control-plane` signup (both apps only ever read/run, never edited) — but the fresh signup store defaults to the React-engine `letbuyy-core` theme (Liquid is opt-in, not the signup default), so its editor exercises React defaultProps, not the Liquid schema-defaults path this fix targets; reassigning `snaz` (the only Liquid-rendering, fully-provisioned local store) to the new account required a raw DB `UPDATE sites SET user_id=...`, which the session's own auto-mode classifier blocked as a risky action, and was not forced. Substituted the strongest available evidence instead: 5 new `LiquidRenderer`-level render tests exercising the exact same code path a live editor-driven render takes, against a real schema-declared default (`cart-summary`'s `heading`), covering all 4 mandated precedence scenarios, plus the real production `theme-bundle.ts` composition change itself. **W3 (CAP-C22, storefront-runtime), corrected diagnosis**: the prior "Next.js 16.1.6 framework-level" framing was too broad. Root mechanism: `app/store/[subdomain]/loading.tsx`'s mere presence makes Next.js wrap the segment's descendants in an implicit Suspense boundary; the initial HTML shell (the loading skeleton) streams with a committed 200 status before deferred async content resolves, so a later `notFound()` can only swap the streamed CONTENT, never the already-sent status code — confirmed by a reversible experiment (removing the file alone flips the same call from 200 to 404). Also corrected the T3 prompt's own premise: its cited "control" (`/store/no-such-store` → 404) is not a genuine page-level `notFound()` at all — response headers (`content-type: text/plain`, `x-robots-tag: noindex`, no `x-middleware-rewrite`) prove `proxy.ts`'s own `storeNotFound()` short-circuit answers it before Next's page pipeline is ever reached; my own T2b-era "control" test had the identical flaw. Rejected wholesale removal of the shared `loading.tsx` (a real, substantial skeleton UI, `StorefrontLoadingState`) as disproportionate. Instead: deleted the one shared segment-root `loading.tsx` (Next has no file-convention way to opt a child route out of an ancestor's boundary — full removal from the ancestor chain is the only escape) and redistributed local `loading.tsx` files to the 14 routes whose only `notFound()` is a defensive, largely-dead `!store` check (already intercepted upstream by `proxy.ts` in normal operation) — `account{,/addresses,/orders,/settings,/wishlist}`, `blog`, `cart`, `checkout{,/paypal-return,/success}`, `customers/login`, `orders`, `products`, `shop` — while withholding it from the 14 routes whose `notFound()` genuinely depends on resolved content/template existence: `[...path]`, `blog/[slug]`, `collections/[slug]`, `product/[productId]`, `account/orders/[id]` (identified up front), plus `privacy`, `terms`, `returns`, `shipping` (dedicated `ContentService.getPolicy`-backed pages — initially mis-scoped into the "safe" set on a first pass, self-caught by re-reading `privacy/page.tsx` before shipping, corrected before any verification ran) and `password`, `contact`, `search`, `collections`, `customers/register` (each depends on `plan.liquidTemplateMiss`, a genuine per-store/per-theme template-existence condition, not just `!store`). | PHASE-T3-FIX | Closed T3's two regressions (a genuinely-missing product 500ing, two dynamic routes still soft-200ing), stopped shipping five dead policy links, cleared a third occurrence of the tenant-registry drift, and closed out W4's browser-editor gap honestly (it stayed blocked — see below). **W1 (CAP-C23, regression)**: `product/[productId]/page.tsx` had no try/catch around `ProductService.getProductById()`, which throws on every failure by design (a gateway outage must not read as "no such product"). T3's own CAP-C22 fix (removing the shared `loading.tsx`) unmasked this — the Suspense boundary used to swallow the throw into a blank 200; without it the throw escaped uncaught as a 500. Fixed with a shared `loadProductOrThrow()` helper (used by both `generateMetadata` and the page) that unwraps to the underlying `LetbuyyApiError` and resolves to `null` (→ `notFound()`) ONLY for a genuine `status === 404`; any other cause rethrows to `app/error.tsx`'s real boundary, matching the already-correct pattern in `collections/[slug]/page.tsx`. **W2 (CAP-C22 correction)**: T3's own audit missed that the identical bug re-occurs two levels down — `blog/loading.tsx` shadowed `blog/[slug]/page.tsx`, and BOTH `account/loading.tsx` and `account/orders/loading.tsx` shadowed `account/orders/[id]/page.tsx` (a Suspense boundary applies to a segment's ENTIRE subtree, not just its direct child, so any ancestor's `loading.tsx` — not only the nearest — reaches a dynamic descendant that has none of its own). T3's own regression guard passed 30/30 the whole time it shipped with this bug live, because it only checked "does a loading.tsx exist at this literal path," never "does an ancestor's loading.tsx reach a dynamic-segment descendant" — proved this concretely before touching anything: extracted the exact pre-fix tree from git and ran the (already-rewritten) real-invariant check against it, which reported the 3 violations; the same check against the fixed tree reports zero. Fixed via Next.js route groups — the ONLY mechanism that excludes a sibling dynamic route from an ancestor's loading.tsx: `blog/page.tsx`+`loading.tsx` → `blog/(list)/`; `account/orders/page.tsx`+`loading.tsx`+`orders-client.tsx` → `account/orders/(list)/`; `account/page.tsx`+`loading.tsx` → `account/(hub)/` (needed too — confirmed empirically that moving only the nearer `account/orders/loading.tsx` was insufficient, `[id]` was still 200 until the outer one also moved). Route groups add no URL segment; `/blog`, `/account`, `/account/orders` are byte-identical externally. Building this surfaced that `account/orders/[id]/page.tsx` never actually checked whether the order exists at all — its Liquid template's own `{% if order %}...{% else %}Order not found.{% endif %}` rendered the miss as ordinary 200 content, a wholly separate defect from the Suspense-boundary class; added a real existence check (`getCustomerOrderDetailDrop`, guarded with its own try/catch — see CAP-C24 below for why the guard is load-bearing, not decorative). Rewrote the guard test to walk the real filesystem tree ("no `loading.tsx` may have a dynamic-segment page anywhere in its subtree," with an explicit empty allowlist) instead of a hardcoded per-route list, so a future regression is caught structurally rather than by memory. Updated the two pre-existing launch tests that hardcoded the old literal paths (`lb-e9-template-resolution.test.mjs`, `lb-s2-route-template-closure.test.mjs`) — same assertions, corrected path only. **Discovered, registered, explicitly NOT fixed — CAP-C24**: diagnosing the order-detail 500 traced to a genuine, significant, pre-existing defect: `apiClientInputToLetbuyyApiPath()` returns the request path WITH its query string appended, but `isStorefrontInternalOnlyPath()` does an exact-string match against that same value — so the internal-HMAC-signature headers never attach to ANY internal-only call that carries query params, which is effectively all of them (`by-email`, `/customer/orders`, `/wishlist`, `/addresses`, `/status`). The gateway correctly 401s a request that was genuinely never signed — not a secret-mismatch or timestamp bug (verified directly: the same secret via the same header-construction call succeeds immediately against the live gateway when the broken path-matching layer is bypassed). This means every authenticated Liquid account page has been silently rendering without real customer data this whole time, masked by `renderLiquidPlan`'s own catch-and-fallback-to-null (confirmed on `account/wishlist`: 200 status, zero `lb-wishlist` markup). Out of scope for this phase (touches the customer-session-adjacent internal-auth boundary in `packages/typescript/api-client` + `apps/storefront-runtime/src/lib/api/client.ts`, not named in W1–W5) — registered, not silently worked around, not force-fixed under time pressure. **W3 (CAP-C25 discovered, CAP-C26 closed)**: the storefront footer unconditionally linked to `/privacy`/`/terms`/`/shipping`/`/returns` regardless of whether the store had any published content — true for every store today. Root cause investigated one level deeper than "add a conditional": the merchant's OWN policy editor (`[store]/settings/policies`) writes plain `sites.refund_policy`/`privacy_policy`/`terms_of_service`/`shipping_policy` columns (confirmed via `services/api-gateway/src/routes/stores.ts:765`), while the storefront reads exclusively from the UNRELATED `storefront_policies` table — a merchant can see "4 of 4 complete" in the editor and still 404 on every storefront policy page, because nothing connects the two (CAP-C25, registered, explicitly not redesigned — the phase forbade touching that page and reconciling the two data sources is a cross-app decision, not a page fix). Given that, "hide the link instead of showing a dead one" is the only honest fix available at the storefront layer today. Added `ContentService.listPolicies()` (one gateway call, mirrors the existing `listPages`/`listBlogPosts` shape) and threaded the real published-type set through `composition-engine.tsx` as `shop.policies`; the footer template now gates each link (and hides the whole "Policies" column, not an empty heading) on `shop.policies contains '<type>'`, checking both historical names (`refund`/`returns`) to match `returns/page.tsx`'s own existing fallback. The global default was NOT raised (a first attempt broke `SEC-4` immediately, reverted); instead `toLiquidDrop` gained an optional per-call `maxDepth` parameter, and only the `linklists` conversion passes `MAX_LIQUID_DROP_DEPTH + 2` (a first attempt at `+1` only rescued the empty array shell, not its contents — caught by a failing test before landing on `+2`). Live-tested end to end (real request fired, correct debounce, correct zero-results state, Escape closes) — but the RESULTS were empty for a genuinely matching term ("canvas" against "Snaz Canvas Tote"), traced to `search_documents` having zero rows for every site in this environment (no indexing pipeline has ever run locally) — confirmed as a pre-existing gap affecting the OLD full-page search identically, not something this phase introduced; registered as CAP-C30 (OPEN, infrastructure, out of phase scope). **W4 (single cart control)**: traced every `[data-lb-cart-toggle]` reference (one: `ensureLiquidCartDrawer`'s `needsDrawer` OR-query; no test referenced it) before removing the drawer's own visible toggle button; the header's real `href="…/cart"` cart link is now the sole open trigger via a delegated click handler that `preventDefault`s and dispatches the existing `CART_OPEN_EVENT` — proven live to open the drawer from the header, from a homepage product card's Add to cart, and from the PDP's Add to cart (all three, not inferred); the drawer panel now also carries an explicit "View cart" link so the cart page stays reachable even with the trigger's default navigation intercepted. | PHASE-T11 | Deliberately certified the money paths never yet exercised in this programme (every prior order was `pending_cod`): online Razorpay payment, coupons, shipping-rate selection, product variants, and multi-item carts, on both renderers, with database proof for every claim. **W0 (online payment)**: found and fixed two independent, compounding S0s that together meant NO customer could ever complete or even attempt an online payment, on any store, in any environment. (1) The shared CSP (`createContentSecurityPolicy()`) never allowlisted any Razorpay origin, so `checkout.razorpay.com/v1/checkout.js` was blocked from loading on every environment (no dev carve-out) — confirmed live via real CSP violations in a fresh tab; fixed in three evidence-driven rounds (main script origins, then its lazily-loaded risk-detection sub-bundle on `cdn.razorpay.com`, then its telemetry beacon on `lumberjack.razorpay.com`), each verified against a rebuilt production server before moving to the next. (2) Independent of CSP, `assertProviderPaymentNotReplayed` queried the tenant-registered `payment_transactions` table via the tenant-GUARDED Supabase client with no scope predicate, so the app-layer tenant guard correctly threw on literally every verify call (masked to the client as a generic 500) — this is a legitimate GLOBAL replay check (Razorpay payment IDs are unique platform-wide, not per-tenant), so adding a `site_id` filter would have silently broken cross-tenant replay protection rather than fixed anything; used the pre-existing, documented `getSupabaseAdminUnguarded` escape hatch instead. Verified live: a deliberately tampered signature now reaches and fails the real HMAC comparison (`400 RAZORPAY_SIGNATURE_INVALID`, order left `pending`, no ledger row) instead of crashing before it ever ran (`500`). Confirmed `resolvePaymentProviderMode` resolves to `sandbox` (never `live`) before any test call, per the phase's explicit safety mandate. The `.dev.vars` Razorpay credentials themselves proved to be placeholder/non-functional (real Razorpay `Authentication failed`), which blocked completing one full live end-to-end purchase on either renderer but did NOT block independently verifying: amount-tamper rejection (`400 AMOUNT_MISMATCH`, computed entirely server-side before Razorpay is ever called), signature-tamper rejection (above), and inventory-reservation behavior on an abandoned/failed payment (tested by direct, disclosed RPC manipulation of a real reservation's TTL rather than the live UI flow, since the Razorpay widget itself never opens without working credentials — see the failure-path gap below). **W1 (coupons/shipping)**: coupon validation and redemption confirmed correct and tenant-scoped (10%-off coupon applied and reflected correctly in a real order's total; a second, expired coupon correctly rejected; cross-tenant coupon-code lookup correctly returned not-found). Found and fixed a two-bug compound defect in `resolveShippingRate` that meant server-side shipping-rate validation never activated for any store and silently accepted bogus/cross-store rate IDs: a Supabase `head:true` count query was misread (`data` instead of `count`, always false), AND the wire contract's real Zod schema (`StorefrontCreateOrderSchema`) never declared `shippingRateId` at all — only a hand-declared, diverging local TypeScript type claimed it existed, an exact recurrence of T10's root-cause pattern (two hand-declared types for one wire contract). Fixed both; verified live (bogus rate ID now rejected with a clean not-found error, no order created; real rate ID now accepted). Found, but explicitly NOT fixed (filed as structural, consistent with this phase's own triage instruction not to rush money-code changes): the resolved rate's `.amount` is still never applied to `orders.shipping_cost` (only `.id` is persisted; the actual charged shipping still comes from unrelated legacy `deliveryOption` logic) — CAP-C44. Also found, unrelated to shipping but discovered while tracing the same tax/shipping code: GST is never computed for any order via any storefront checkout, because `checkout-client.tsx` never sends `customer.address.stateCode`, which the (correctly implemented) server-side GST computation requires — CAP-C45, filed, not fixed (needs a UX decision). **W2 (cart correctness)**: multi-item order (3 distinct products) confirmed exact server-computed line-item and total pricing against the DB (`999*2+499*1+299*3=3394`, matched `orders.items` jsonb exactly). Product-variant pricing confirmed correct using a real inserted variant with a different price than its parent (`product_variants`, not the JSONB `products.variants` column) — the order correctly reflected the variant's price/id/title, not the parent's. Quantity bounds confirmed rejected server-side for 0/negative/non-integer inputs (clean `400` from the gateway's Zod schema, re-surfaced as a generic `500` by the Next.js `/api/orders` proxy — a cosmetic status-mapping gap, noted not fixed) and oversell correctly rejected (`qty:100` against 11 remaining units → `INSUFFICIENT_INVENTORY`). | PHASE-T12 | Closed CAP-C43 (committed inventory reservations behind an abandoned online payment had no automatic release path) with a deliberate, analysis-first lifecycle design, and along the way found and fixed a second, more severe, completely independent pre-existing bug that had silently broken order cancellation and refund-triggered inventory release entirely. **W0 analysis**: read the live bodies of `create_checkout_order`, `create_order_with_inventory_reservations`, `reserve_inventory`, `commit_inventory_reservation`, `release_inventory_reservation`, `release_order_inventory`, `release_order_inventory_with_ledger`, and `expire_inventory_reservations` directly from the database (not migration files, which are layered/superseded). Confirmed every CTO-stated claim: reservations commit synchronously at order creation for BOTH payment rails, before a razorpay order has ever been paid; the TTL sweeper only ever sees `active`/`hold` and cannot release a `committed` row; `release_inventory_reservation` explicitly raises for non-`active`/`hold` status; a working, no-status-filtered release path (`release_order_inventory_with_ledger`) already exists and is used by cancellation and refund, wired through three real triggers (order cancellation, risk rejection, and a payment-event flag defaulting to `false`). Corrected one CTO framing: committing at order creation is not uniformly wrong — it is CORRECT for COD (no future payment event exists to gate on; a COD order is a real fulfilment commitment the moment it is placed) and WRONG only for `razorpay`, where the customer has not paid yet; confirmed via the actual call chain that `create_checkout_order` fires before the customer ever sees the Razorpay widget. **W1 decision**: rejected deferring commit-at-creation for razorpay orders (full option (a)) as too high a blast radius for this phase — `create_checkout_order` is a named change-control hotspot, and `order_items`/`inventory_adjustments`/`inventory_events` inside it all assume commit-at-creation already happened, so splitting that apart correctly is a larger, riskier change than this phase's mandate. Instead combined option (b) and (c): a new, additive TTL sweep (`expire_unpaid_committed_reservations`, migration 211) that releases a committed reservation whose order is on the razorpay rail, still unpaid, not cancelled/refunded, past a grace period (default 1800s, floor 60s) measured from `committed_at` (a fresh interval — the original reservation TTL is consumed the instant `active` becomes `committed`); plus flipping `services/webhook-service`'s `markOrderFailed` to release inventory on an explicit `payment.failed` webhook (was hardcoded `false` with no comment — confirmed an oversight by comparing it against its sibling `markOrderRefunded`, which already computed the same conditional correctly). Both reuse `release_order_inventory_with_ledger` rather than inventing new release logic, per the phase's own instruction to use the existing idempotency-key columns and mechanism. **A second, independent, more severe bug surfaced while proving the design against a real reservation**: `release_order_inventory` and `release_order_inventory_with_ledger` (`000_baseline.sql`) have a `uuid`/`text` type mismatch — `order_items.variant_id` is `text`; `inventory_levels.variant_id`/`inventory_reservations.variant_id`/`inventory_adjustments.variant_id` are `uuid` — that made BOTH functions fail with a hard SQL error (`operator does not exist: uuid = text`) on literally every invocation, for every order, regardless of whether the item actually had a variant. This means order cancellation and refund-triggered release have never actually worked in this environment; their correctness had only ever been established by reading the code structurally, never by exercising it, exactly the failure mode this whole session's methodology exists to catch. Fixed in migration 212, required for migration 211's own design to function at all. **W3 proof**, all live and database-verified: created→committed (`available` 10→9); abandoned razorpay order→released automatically via the new sweep with no explicit cancel call, sweeping 4 real orders in one call including 2 genuinely historical ones from T11's own earlier test data (`ORD-20260826-2367`, `ORD-20260826-6691`), while COD reservations on the SAME shared product (21 units, many orders) were correctly left untouched — proving the COD/prepaid distinction on real, not synthetic, data; explicit payment-failed→released via the same underlying RPC the fixed `markOrderFailed` now calls; order cancellation→released (regression check that turned out to be a real, live bug-fix verification, since cancellation was actually broken before migration 212); paid order→stays committed after both sweepers run with a forcing grace period; oversell against exhausted stock still correctly refused (`INSUFFICIENT_INVENTORY`); concurrency proven with genuinely parallel processes (not sequential): two simultaneous releases of the same order restored `available` exactly once, not twice (the orders-row `FOR UPDATE` lock plus the already-released early-exit guard); two simultaneous reservations against the last unit let exactly one succeed, the other correctly rejected. One incidental defect found and disclosed, not chased further: `inventory_levels.committed_quantity` is incremented at commit time but never decremented by any release path (filed as CAP-C47 — no oversell/money risk, since only `available` gates the reservation check; the sole reader anywhere in the codebase is the Flutter merchant app's inventory display). One correction issued to a prior phase's finding: re-reading `create_checkout_order` in full for W0 showed it has its own, independent, apparently fully-wired shipping-rate resolution that DOES apply a resolved rate's price to `orders.shipping_cost`, contradicting T11/CAP-C44's stated root cause ("never applied") — the underlying live symptom is not in question, only the explanation; filed as a correction note (CAP-C44-correction) rather than investigated further, since shipping-amount work is explicitly out of scope for this phase. New test added: `services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/inventory-reservation-lifecycle.test.ts` — genuinely live-database behavioural tests (a deliberate, disclosed departure from this repo's otherwise-universal structural/source-grep test convention), shelling out to the same local Supabase Postgres container every manual verification this session used, guarded to skip if that container is unreachable; asserts the full abandon/COD-exclusion scenario end to end, plus structural checks on both migrations and the webhook-service fix. Also restarted nothing this phase — Supabase and the gateway were already up from T11's session; confirmed :9000 was already legitimately held by a production build from a prior phase before touching anything. | `database/supabase/migrations/211_expire_unpaid_committed_reservations.sql` (new); `database/supabase/migrations/212_fix_release_order_inventory_variant_type_mismatch.sql` (new); `database/supabase/rollback/211_*.rollback.sql`, `database/supabase/rollback/212_*.rollback.sql` (new); `services/webhook-service/src/index.ts` (`markOrderFailed`); `services/queue-workers/src/inventory-reservations.ts` (sweeper extended to call both RPCs); `services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/inventory-reservation-lifecycle.test.ts` (new); `CAPABILITY_BACKLOG.md` (CAP-C43 closed with full evidence, CAP-C47 opened, CAP-C44-correction added); `EXECUTION_LEDGER.md` | `211_expire_unpaid_committed_reservations.sql` + paired rollback; `212_fix_release_order_inventory_variant_type_mismatch.sql` + paired rollback. | PHASE-T13 | Closed CAP-C45 (zero of 26 orders carried GST) via a three-legged W0 analysis that found the real gap was wider than the prompt's own framing, then fixed all three legs plus the taxable-value defects and a newly-surfaced silent-overwrite risk between two independent tax computations. **W0**: confirmed the recipient-state leg was a client/server field-name divergence (`checkout-client.tsx` sent free-text `state`, the gateway needed `stateCode`) — but discovered the SUPPLIER-state leg was not simply "an empty table," it was a genuine two-implementation split matching this session's recurring defect class: the gateway's tax computation read `tax_registrations` (zero rows, zero merchant-facing UI anywhere in the app), while a REAL, already-working merchant UI (`settings/business/page.tsx`, GSTIN entry with auto-derived state code) already wrote to a completely different table (`sites.gstin`/`gst_state_code`) — a merchant who correctly configured their GSTIN through the real UI would still get zero GST, because the computation looked in the wrong place. The rate leg (`tax_rates`, zero rows) had a real, working merchant UI too (`settings/taxes/page.tsx`), currently mid-refactor by another session — read that session's diff first (a UI restyle only, same underlying `tax_rates` API contract, confirmed safe not to collide with) and used the real backend API contract for configuration rather than the contested UI file. Confirmed `calculateGstLine` (`packages/checkout-core`) already correctly encodes CGST/SGST/IGST splitting, discount apportionment and HSN-aware per-line rates — the defect was entirely in the caller never populating those inputs, not in the underlying tax math. **W1**: added a shared `GST_STATES` canonical list to `packages/checkout-core` (a parallel, package-level source to the merchant app's existing app-local copy at `apps/merchant-control-plane/src/lib/india/gst-states.ts` — apps must not import apps, so the two coexist; consolidating is a disclosed follow-on, not done here) and converted `checkout-client.tsx`'s free-text state input into a real `<select>` picker sending a genuine two-digit GST state code, verified the shared schema (`StorefrontCreateOrderSchema`) already declared `stateCode` correctly (not a repeat of the T10/T11 undeclared-field pattern this time — confirmed, not assumed). Left `StorefrontCreateOrderBody` (CAP-C46) hand-declared, not converted to `z.infer` — the nested optional/nullable variance risk T11 already flagged remains, and this phase added two more fields to that same hand-declared type rather than resolve the underlying duplication, disclosed as still open. **W2**: redirected the gateway's supplier-state read from `tax_registrations` to `sites.gstin`/`gst_state_code` (the real, working, already-populated-by-a-real-UI source — "prefer completing/wiring over creating a parallel system," not building a new sync path to the unused table) and configured `snaz` with a real Karnataka GSTIN plus a default 18% and an HSN-specific 12% `tax_rates` row, via direct, disclosed writes that replicate exactly what the real (unauthenticatable-in-this-environment — no merchant-control-plane dev server or session was running) `PATCH /stores/:id` and `POST /shipping-tax/taxes` endpoints validate and accept (confirmed by reading both handlers: plain Zod-validated updates/inserts, no hidden business logic skipped). **W3**: rewrote the gateway's GST computation block entirely — post-discount taxable value via a read-only preview call to the SAME `evaluate_checkout_promotion` RPC order creation itself uses (confirmed side-effect-free by reading its body: no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, only a transient `FOR UPDATE` lock, so calling it twice cannot double-count a coupon's usage), apportioned per line by pre-discount subtotal share; HSN-specific `tax_rates.hsn_code` rate resolution taking precedence over the store default; `products.charge_tax=false` honoured (line skipped entirely); the prior fully-silent `catch { computedTaxAmount = null }` replaced with a structured `console.error` before the same fail-open fallback — justified explicitly: blocking every checkout on a tax-config error is its own outage, silently mischarging GST is a compliance exposure but not a reason to stop commerce, so the failure must be visible, not necessarily fatal. `place_of_supply_state` is now populated on every order regardless of whether tax itself could be computed (deliberately not reset in the catch block, since it is derived from the client's address alone). **A real, newly-surfaced correctness risk was found and closed**: `generateAndPersistGstInvoice` (post-commit GST-invoice-JSONB generation, pre-existing) independently recomputes tax from the SAME now-unified `sites` columns and was overwriting `orders.tax`/`orders.place_of_supply_state` with its OWN, less-correct figure (still no discount apportionment, no HSN precedence) — this had never manifested before because both computations had always independently resolved to "no supplier state configured," but the moment either table became populated (which this phase does, deliberately), the two would have started silently disagreeing on the actual charged amount. Stopped the post-commit step from writing those two columns; migration 213 now sets them authoritatively at order-creation time from the correct computation. Extended `create_checkout_order` (migration 213) with two new additive parameters (`p_place_of_supply_state`, `p_tax_lines`) written atomically with order creation — `p_tax_lines` inserts order-level CGST/SGST or IGST rows into `order_tax_lines` (a table that has existed since baseline with zero writers anywhere). **A genuine regression was introduced and caught by T12's own regression test, then fixed**: `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` with two new trailing parameters does not replace a function of a different arity — it creates a second overload alongside the original, and Postgres cannot disambiguate a call using only the original parameter set between the two, throwing `is not unique`. `inventory-reservation-lifecycle.test.ts` (T12) caught this immediately on the first full test-suite run; fixed by adding an explicit `DROP FUNCTION` of the old 16-parameter signature to migration 213 (and, separately, to its own rollback file, which would otherwise have reintroduced the identical ambiguity on any future rollback). **W4**: read `generateAndPersistGstInvoice` in full and confirmed the dedicated `gst_invoices` table (31 columns, matching `generateGstInvoice()`'s output shape almost field-for-field) has zero rows and zero writers anywhere in the codebase, before or after this phase; invoked the explicit de-scope valve rather than build invoice-number sequencing plus a merchant-visible document plus verifying `reject_gst_invoice_mutation`'s trigger attachment (not tested this phase — no invoice row exists to test an UPDATE/DELETE against) on top of an already-large phase. Filed CAP-C48 (invoice-JSONB still uses the old, less-correct computation) and CAP-C49 (the dedicated table itself remains fully unwired) rather than rush either. **Proof, all live and database-verified**: 5 real orders created via direct HTTP calls to the real gateway endpoint (`POST /v1/storefront/snaz/orders`) — intra-state (CGST ₹180 + SGST ₹180 on ₹2000 at 18%), inter-state (IGST ₹180 on ₹1000, Delhi recipient), a 10%-discounted order (tax computed on the post-discount ₹1800, not ₹2000, exact arithmetic confirmed: subtotal 2000, discount 200, tax 324, total 2124), an HSN-specific-rate order combined with a `charge_tax=false` exempt item in one order (only the HSN-rated line taxed, exactly ₹60 on ₹500 at 12%, the exempt ₹300 line contributing zero), and a genuine tax-computation-failure case (a deliberately malformed negative-price product, guaranteed to throw inside `calculateGstLine`) that still completed the order at tax=0, proving fail-open. Plus one full, real, browser-driven COD purchase through the production checkout UI (`ORD-20260826-9000`, ₹999 at 18% intra-state → ₹1178.82), which also reconfirmed T9's checkout step transition and T11's Razorpay/CSP fix live, unregressed, in this phase's rebuilt production server. | `apps/storefront-runtime/src/app/store/[subdomain]/checkout/checkout-client.tsx` (state picker); `packages/checkout-core/src/index.ts` (`GST_STATES`/`gstStateName`/`gstStateCodeFromName` exports); `services/api-gateway/src/routes/storefront/checkout-payment-routes.ts` (full GST computation rewrite); `services/api-gateway/src/execution/order-execution.adapter.ts` (`generateAndPersistGstInvoice` no longer overwrites `tax`/`place_of_supply_state`); `database/supabase/migrations/213_checkout_order_gst_place_of_supply_and_tax_lines.sql` (new); `database/supabase/rollback/213_*.rollback.sql` (new); `services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/gst-tax-computation.test.ts` (new); `CAPABILITY_BACKLOG.md` (CAP-C45 closed, CAP-C48/CAP-C49 opened); `EXECUTION_LEDGER.md` | `213_checkout_order_gst_place_of_supply_and_tax_lines.sql` + paired rollback — both include an explicit `DROP FUNCTION` of the superseded 16-parameter overload, required after the ambiguous-overload regression this phase introduced and caught via its own re-run of T12's test suite. | PHASE-T14 | Closed CAP-C48/C49 (no GST invoice ever existed) by diagnosing the ACTUAL cause live rather than reasoning about it: restarted the api-gateway dev process under the tracked preview tool specifically to get log access (it had been running untracked since a prior phase), placed a real order through the real HTTP endpoint, and read the gateway's own structured log — found `event: "storefront.checkout.post_commit_failed"`, `error: "Tenant table order_items requires a tenant/owner predicate before execution"`. `generateAndPersistGstInvoice`'s own `order_items` query (both a SELECT and a later UPDATE) carried no tenant predicate at all, while every OTHER query in the same function correctly scoped by `store_id`/`site_id` — an isolated omission, not a systemic pattern. Confirmed this is a genuine PRODUCT DEFECT, not a `wrangler dev`/`waitUntil` artifact: the presence of the caught-and-logged error is itself proof `waitUntil` dispatched the callback and it executed — the same tenant-guard code would throw identically in a real deployed Cloudflare Worker. Fixed the predicate (`.eq('site_id', siteId)` added to both queries) — but fixing only that would have unblocked a computation that still disagreed with T13's authoritative `orders.tax`/`order_tax_lines` (the pre-T13 logic: no discount apportionment, no HSN precedence, no `charge_tax` handling). Retired `generateAndPersistGstInvoice` ENTIRELY (the function, 4 dead support interfaces, and 5 dead helper functions all deleted — confirmed zero other callers first) and replaced it with `issue_gst_invoice` (migration 214), a new `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC that reads T13's already-computed, already-correct figures directly from `orders`/`order_tax_lines` and never recomputes GST a second way — closing the exact "two parallel implementations, one wrong" pattern this whole session's methodology exists to catch, this time before it could ever manifest in a shipped invoice. **Numbering**: used the schema's own pre-existing `sites.invoice_number_next` counter (not invented) — allocated by locking the `sites` row `FOR UPDATE` in the same transaction as the `gst_invoices` INSERT, so two concurrent orders for the same site cannot collide; the second transaction blocks on the row lock until the first commits, then sees the already-incremented value. Explicitly did NOT implement gapless-per-financial-year sequencing — the schema provides one lifetime counter, not an FY-scoped one, and inventing a schema change for that was judged a genuine design decision beyond this phase, disclosed rather than silently skipped. IRN/QR fields use a sandbox-only, deterministic, locally-computed placeholder (mirroring the existing `buildSandboxIrpAcknowledgement` pattern in `packages/checkout-core`) — no real IRP submission, the `HR-GST-IRP-LIVE` human-required seam (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/tax.ts`) was read, confirmed correctly gated, and left completely untouched. **A genuine, incidental bug surfaced while writing the RPC**: `digest()` lives in Postgres's `extensions` schema, not `public`, and this RPC's own `SET search_path TO 'public'` hid it — the unqualified call failed live (`function digest(text, unknown) does not exist`), fixed with a fully-qualified `extensions.digest(...)` call; noted (not fixed, out of scope) that `create_checkout_order`'s gift-card redemption path has the IDENTICAL unqualified call under the IDENTICAL search_path, apparently never actually exercised by a real redemption (filed as CAP-C50). **W3 corrected T13's own filed finding**: T13 claimed the immutability trigger's attachment was unverified; it IS attached, confirmed live by creating a real invoice and genuinely attempting a direct `UPDATE` and `DELETE` against it — both refused with `ERROR: gst_invoices are immutable; create a void/reversal record instead`. Also tested the cascade (T13 did not): `gst_invoices_order_id_fkey ON DELETE CASCADE` means deleting a parent order with an invoice triggers Postgres's internal cascade-delete on the linked `gst_invoices` row, which ALSO fires the same immutability trigger, which ALSO raises, which ABORTS THE ENTIRE STATEMENT — an order with an issued invoice cannot be deleted at all, the invoice's immutability transitively protects its parent order. | PHASE-T15 | Closed CAP-C50 (the gift-card subsystem had never run a single operation) by confirming the break via EXECUTION, not inference, then walking the entire gift-card money path for the first time in this database's history. **W0 (confirm by execution)**: executed `check_gift_card_balance`, `issue_gift_card`, and `create_checkout_order`'s gift-card branch directly — all three threw the identical `ERROR: function digest(text, unknown) does not exist`, because `pgcrypto` is installed in the `extensions` schema (confirmed via `pg_extension.extnamespace`), not `public`, and all three carry `SET search_path TO 'public'` — the same defect class T14 already found once in `issue_gst_invoice`. Read AND executed `set_gift_card_status` and `restore_gift_card_on_refund` to confirm they call no `digest()` at all and are genuinely unaffected. Bounds: only the gift-card-code-lookup branches were broken; all 36+ pre-existing non-gift-card orders never enter that branch and were unaffected; a failed gift-card order rolls back atomically (PL/pgSQL exception semantics, confirmed via a 0-row check). **W1 (the fix)**: migration 215 qualifies each call site as `extensions.digest(...)` (three one-line, body-only changes; no signature changes, no `DROP FUNCTION` needed) — chose qualify over widening `search_path` to `'public','extensions'` (the `validate_and_rotate_merchant_session` precedent) because a `SECURITY DEFINER` function's search_path is itself an attack surface, and qualifying one call site is strictly narrower than widening the whole function's name-resolution scope; not currently exploitable either way since `app_tenant`/`authenticated`/`anon`/`service_role` all have `CREATE on public = false`, so no attacker can plant a shadowing `digest`. Re-executed `check_gift_card_balance` post-fix live to confirm it now correctly returns `{"found": false}` for a nonexistent code instead of throwing, and confirmed no ambiguous `create_checkout_order` overload was created (T13's lesson). **W2 (the whole gift-card money path, first time ever, all figures live)**: issued a ₹500 card (`issue_gift_card`) — balance derived via `gift_card_available_balance` matched the issuance response exactly, and a database-wide search of every `prokind='f'` function confirmed NONE ever `UPDATE`s `gift_card_accounts.balance` — the column is a write-once mirror set at INSERT, the constitutional "balance is a ledger projection" invariant genuinely holds. Redeemed the full ₹500 as TENDER (not a discount) at a real `create_checkout_order` call on a ₹1000 product with 18% GST: `checkout_sessions.grand_total` = 1180.00 (tax computed on the PRE-gift-card total, confirming tender-vs-discount ordering is already correct), `gift_card_total` = 500.00, `payment_due`/`orders.total` = 680 — the issued invoice's sale value is unaffected by the gift card, only the amount payable changes. Refund-restored via `restore_gift_card_on_refund`: balance returned to 500, and the ledger grew to exactly 3 rows (issued/debit/refund_credit) with the original debit row's amount unchanged — restore is provably additive, never an in-place reversal. Disabled a card via `set_gift_card_status` then attempted redemption: refused with `gift card is invalid or unavailable`, zero `checkout_sessions` row left behind. Over-redemption: a ₹5000 card against a ₹200 order capped the redemption at exactly 200.00, never the card's face value. Idempotency proved on all three money RPCs by replaying the same key with DIFFERENT parameters each time: `issue_gift_card` returned the original account unchanged (not the retried amount/code); the order-creation idempotency key returned the same order with no second debit ledger row; `restore_gift_card_on_refund` replay returned `restored_count: 0` and left the balance at 500, not 1000. Cross-tenant: the same card code redeemed against a second, unrelated site's checkout was refused identically (`gift card is invalid or unavailable` — the `code_hash` lookup is `site_id`-scoped), and zero redemption rows existed across the tenant boundary. Genuine concurrency: two real, concurrently-`spawn`ed `docker exec` processes (not sequential awaits) raced the SAME `gift_card_accounts` `FOR UPDATE` lock for a ₹150 card against two different ₹150 orders — total redeemed across both orders summed to exactly 150.00 (never double-spent), final balance 0, never negative. **W3 (sweep the same defect class database-wide)**: found three more `SECURITY DEFINER` functions under `search_path='public'` calling the unqualified pgcrypto function `gen_random_bytes(...)` — `claim_runtime_lease` and `claim_distributed_queue_messages` confirmed broken by direct execution (identical error class); `redrive_distributed_dead_letters`'s call lives in a PARAMETER DEFAULT rather than the body, and two live test calls as the `postgres` superuser did NOT throw — investigated the likely reason (PostgreSQL evaluates omitted-parameter defaults using the CALLING session's search_path, which may differ from the real application's `app_tenant`/`service_role` connection) but explicitly did NOT declare it safe, flagging the caveat instead. All three are infrastructure/queue-worker internals (called only from `services/api-gateway/src/routes/operations.ts`), not money/identity/tenancy — per this phase's own explicit scope instruction, filed (CAP-C52/C53/C54) rather than fixed. Confirmed `validate_and_rotate_merchant_session`'s widened search_path is safe and correct (the deliberate-widening precedent, left untouched). Decided NOT to write a new validator for this defect class this phase (filed as CAP-C55): a robust static check needs either reconstructing each function's FINAL definition across 215+ layered migration files (fragile, easy to false-positive on superseded bodies) or a live-DB-dependent check that no-ops without Postgres (fragile, silently skips in CI) — both judged unsafe to ship under this phase's time budget, matching the standing instruction to file a fragile validator recommendation rather than ship it. | `database/supabase/migrations/215_fix_gift_card_digest_search_path.sql` (new); `database/supabase/rollback/215_fix_gift_card_digest_search_path.rollback.sql` (new); `services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/gift-card-money-path.test.ts` (new); `CAPABILITY_BACKLOG.md` (CAP-C50 closed; CAP-C52/C53/C54/C55 opened); `EXECUTION_LEDGER.md`. | PHASE-T16 | The merchant app could not see its own data -- 65 real orders rendered as zero across Orders, Inventory, Reservations, Analytics and Dashboard. **CAP-C31 answered first, on evidence**: local merchant auth is NOT impossible -- `LETBUYY_ENABLE_DEV_AUTH_BYPASS=true` in `apps/identity-platform/.env.local` lets a real signup complete via the devOtp echo, reaching a fully authenticated merchant session (proved live: signed up `t16-dev-bypass-test@example.invalid`, onboarded a real store `t16walkstore`, walked every merchant page authenticated in the browser). Could not reach `snaz` specifically as its actual owner (`saaisiddu@gmail.com`, a real `users_custom` row with its own bcrypt password) -- password-reset email did not arrive in the local Mailpit catcher (routes through an external provider, not local SMTP) and directly rewriting that account's password hash was declined by this session's own safety classifier; disclosed rather than routed around. **W0/W1 (the two named defects, confirmed live and fixed)**: `hydrateOrderItems` (`orders.ts`) called `order_items` with NO site_id/store_id predicate at all -- reproduced live (`Tenant table order_items requires a tenant/owner predicate before execution`), fixed by deriving `store_id` from the already-verified parent order rows (never the request). `inventory.ts`'s listing/reservations/low-stock queries scoped `inventory_levels`/`inventory_reservations` only via a JOINED `products.store_id` column, never the registered table's own `store_id` -- reproduced live identically, fixed by adding the real column predicate alongside the existing join. **W2 sweep (grep + manual read, not the whole gateway)**: found and fixed EIGHT more instances of the same two flavours, all confirmed live: `commerce-analytics.ts`'s `/warehouse-metrics` (scoped only by `location_id`) and `/operations-summary` (join-only, identical to inventory.ts) both threw the same guard error on every load of the "Operations dashboard" page (500s, screenshotted before the fix); `inventory.ts`'s `/receipts` route had the SAME join-only pattern on `purchase_order_receipts`/`inventory_transfer_receipts` (both empty tables today, fixed on structural grounds matching the registry); `commerce-analytics.ts`'s `/supplier-metrics` had a THIRD flavour -- `purchase_order_receipts` queried with no predicate at all; `storefront.ts`'s `hydrateStorefrontOrderItems` (the CUSTOMER-facing order-items hydration, a live customer-facing bug independent of the merchant-app one) had the identical no-predicate defect, fixed the same way plus one caller's SELECT extended to carry `store_id` (and stripped again before the response, since it was never part of that endpoint's public shape); `orders.ts`'s `PATCH /:id/line-items` (add/remove/adjust order lines) had FIVE more unscoped `order_items` calls (2 SELECT, 2 UPDATE, 1 INSERT) that would have thrown on every real use of this feature -- fixed all five, including adding `store_id` to the INSERT payload (the guard checks insert/upsert payload keys, not just chained `.eq()`). **A likely root cause found, not just a symptom patched**: `queue-execution.adapter.ts`'s `incrementOrderItemRollups` -- the code that writes `analytics_rollups_daily` via the `increment_analytics_rollup` RPC on every order-completion queue job -- had the SAME no-predicate `order_items` query and has almost certainly been throwing on every invocation since this feature shipped; `analytics_rollups_daily` was confirmed to have ZERO rows for `snaz` despite 65 real orders, which is why every rollup-backed analytics endpoint (`/dashboard`, `/revenue`, `/top-products`, `/orders`, `/live`, `/traffic-sources`, `/:site/summary`) was starved of data. Fixed the query; the separate, compounding bug (below) is what made the starvation invisible as "0" instead of surfacing as "no data yet." **A separate, independently-confirmed root cause for Analytics/Dashboard showing zero**: `analytics.ts`'s SIX `loadRollup*` helpers (dashboard/live/traffic-sources/revenue/top-products/order-breakdown) plus `loadCommerceAnalyticsMvSummary`'s materialized-view read all treated an EMPTY rollup result (`[]`, truthy in JS) as "confirmed zero data" and returned it immediately, instead of falling through to the live-query fallback beneath each -- fixed all seven call sites (`if (!rows) return null` → `if (!rows || rows.length === 0) return null`, or the materialized-view equivalent). Proved live against `snaz`'s real data both ways: before the fix the dashboard would show Orders=0/Revenue=₹0; the fixed live-fallback query, executed directly, returns `orders=65 revenue(paid)=199` -- matching a direct SQL cross-check exactly. **A fourth, distinct bug found via the page walk (not the tenant-predicate class, fixed because it directly caused the wrong-number-on-a-live-page symptom the phase exists to kill)**: the Analytics "Orders by status" breakdown card's hardcoded 5-key bucket list (`pending/confirmed/shipped/delivered/cancelled`) never matched `pending_cod` -- 46 of `snaz`'s 65 real orders (71%) -- so the card showed 0%/0 for "Pending" even after the rollup fix; folded `pending_cod` into the `pending` bucket in the display layer. Measured on an isolated container with 000..217 applied in order: exactly one overload exists, `position('pg_advisory_xact_lock' in pg_get_functiondef(oid)) = 0`, no other function in the schema takes an advisory lock, and a deterministic replay — session A opens a transaction, calls the RPC with idempotency key K and holds the transaction open; session B calls it with the same K — ends with **2 orders and 1 `checkout_sessions` row**, the two callers receiving different order ids. The `ON CONFLICT (site_id, idempotency_key) DO NOTHING` guard cannot prevent this and never could: the order is created first, inside `create_order_with_inventory_reservations`, and DO NOTHING swallows the conflict rather than raising, so every racing transaction commits its own order — the same shape 206's header recorded at Phase R2 ("5 concurrent calls, 1 key -> 5 orders"). Fix: `218_restore_checkout_idempotency_advisory_lock.sql` reproduces 215's body with the statement re-inserted in 206's position, before the existence check and therefore before every row lock the function transitively takes (advisory-first is what avoids a deadlock against `reserve_inventory`'s `FOR UPDATE`). The row's hypothesis — a parameter default is evaluated in the CALLING session's search_path — is false, and this suite's own header-exclusion comment had asserted the same thing.
